describes: Which outside skills this repository wants on every machine: the Claude Code plugins it enables (`claudeEnabledPlugins`), the marketplace each comes from and the tag it is pinned to (`claudePluginMarketplaces`), and the skills the `skills` CLI installs, each pinned to a commit and admitted by an assessment and a skills.sh audit (`installedSkills`); with the bounds the admission and the sync read (`skillAssessorMaxFindings`, `skillAuditTimeoutSeconds`).
whyThisFileExists: A plugin or an installed skill is another repository's text loaded into every session here, so the lists of them are constants with a reason beside each row, and a change to them waits for a person's merge. They share one record, apart from the rest of the policy, so that protecting this one file protects every admission and every removal. `.claude/settings.json` is rendered from this record's `claudeEnabledPlugins` by `tools/integrations/claude.mjs`, because the renderer owns that file and refuses a hand edit to it.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run skills:check refuses an enabled plugin whose marketplace has no source or a source with no tag, a marketplace tag that differs from the mise pin it is held to, a marketplace no enabled plugin uses, an installed skill with no full commit or no reason, one whose name a tracked skill under `.harness/skills/` already holds, one whose assessment read another commit than its pin, one whose assessment or accepted audit found something and names no issue, and a `skill-assessor` agent given any tool but Read, Grep and Glob. mise run skills:selftest holds each of those refusals and the sync over stubs.
whatItDoesNOTDo: It installs nothing: `scripts/skill-sources.mjs sync` makes a machine match it, through `mise run skills:install` or `mise run bootstrap`. It holds no skill the repository writes itself, which live under `.harness/skills/`, and no person's own user-scope plugins or personal skills.
provenance: Added with the skill-management plan (`plans/skill-management-plan-generic.md` in the template's source repository). The Template enables no plugin and installs no skill; a Target project adds rows through the `add-skill` skill.
claudeEnabledPluginsMeans: Each Claude Code plugin this repository enables, as `<plugin>@<marketplace>`, rendered into `.claude/settings.json` `enabledPlugins` and installed at project scope for each clone by `scripts/skill-sources.mjs sync`. Removing an entry uninstalls this clone's project record at the next sync. Each marketplace named must have a row in `claudePluginMarketplaces`.
claudePluginMarketplacesMeans: Each plugin marketplace an enabled plugin comes from, keyed by its name as `claude plugin marketplace list` gives it. A row is `{"source": "<owner>/<repo>#<tag>", "heldTo": "<mise tool>" (optional), "means": "<why>"}`. The tag pins what the marketplace serves, and sync registers it as `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#<tag>`. `heldTo` names a `mise.toml` tool shipped from the same repository, whose pin the tag must equal, with or without a leading `v`, so the plugin and its CLI move together. Where it loses: an upstream fix reaches no machine until someone moves the tag by hand.
installedSkillsMeans: Each skill the `skills` CLI installs into `.claude/skills/<name>/`, keyed by the skill's name. A row is `{"source": "<owner>/<repo>", "commit": "<40-hex sha>", "reason": "<why this repository wants it>", "assessment": {"commit": "<the sha it read>", "rulesCommit": "<the sha of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md it judged against>", "findings": <count>, "issue": "<tracker id, when findings or the audit was not all pass>"}, "audit": {"<provider slug>": {"status": "pass|warn|fail", "riskLevel": "<level>", "auditedAt": "<time>"}}}`. `audit` is the skills.sh result the operator accepted; a sync holds the skill when a provider's result is worse at `fail`, HIGH or CRITICAL, and warns below that. The commit pins the text, since without one the CLI downloads from Vercel's server unchecked. Rows are added only by the `add-skill` skill's admission steps.
skillAssessorMaxFindingsMeans: The most findings the `skill-assessor` agent reports for one skill, ranked most severe first. A finding past this is not reported, so the operator reads a list short enough to decide on. 10 is unmeasured: it is the order of the rubric's six kinds of conflict with room for two of the commonest. Where it loses: a skill with more real conflicts than this shows only the first ten, and the eleventh waits for the next pin move.
skillAuditTimeoutSecondsMeans: How long `scripts/skill-sources.mjs` waits for one skills.sh audit before it treats the audit as unreadable and keeps the accepted result. Every sync reads each installed skill's audit, and a sync runs at each container start and after each pull, so an outage of skills.sh must cost seconds, not stop a machine. Unmeasured; one real read on 2026-10-12 answered well under a second. Where it loses: a slow skills.sh answer past this is read as an outage, so a worsened audit goes unseen until a faster run.
